A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 20-page versions of Optimal Partial Graph Matching. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-keypoint and PPI graph-matching experiments, parameter-sensitivity analyses, and inference-time measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original graph-matching experiments and reports revised OPGM-rs benchmark and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 7 changes L_bias from squared-error supervision of both matched and unmatched nodes to indicator-weighted penalties applied only to matched nodes. This removes direct suppression of unmatched-node biases. The architecture, transport objective, cost loss, and assignment solver remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pascal VOC Keypoint, SPair-71K, IMCPT 50/100, and yeast PPI matching with 5–25% added interactions. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same NGM-v2 and GCAN combinations with dummy, ILP, AFAT-U, and AFAT-I matching methods. The PPI comparisons retain SIGMA and StableGM, and the timing comparison retains the same methods.

E3.justification: Figure 2 narrows the reported sensitivity grids: v3 omits rho=0.35 for both datasets and lambda=0.3 for IMCPT 100. This establishes a limited change in reported sweep settings; benchmark protocols and Appendix B's hyperparameter-search ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing rho/lambda sensitivity analyses receive revised evidence: the plotted rho optimum shifts from 0.35 to 0.4, and SPair-71K shows greater sensitivity at very small lambda. Updated benchmark rows also revise the fixed-versus-learned-bias comparison. No new analysis family is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random starts and 95% confidence intervals for image-keypoint results. Tables and sensitivity plots retain uncertainty reporting; changed interval widths are numerical-result changes, not changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Alongside the loss revision, OPGM-rs mean F1 changes from 57.3 to 57.8 on SPair-71K, 72.8 to 72.7 on IMCPT 50, 72.5 to 72.7 on IMCPT 100, and 60.6 to 60.9 on Pascal VOC. Class scores, confidence bounds, and sensitivity curves also change. Reported inference time changes from 117.5 to 117.8 ms. Baseline, fixed-bias OPGM, and PPI table results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of L_bias in Section 7 changes substantively by removing unmatched-node squared penalties. The transport definitions, optimality and equivalence theorems, complexity argument, and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: weighted-total-variation partial matching, an exact cubic-time assignment solution, and an end-to-end learning architecture with partial matching loss. Their claimed scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 replaces the explanation that bias supervision pushes unmatched nodes toward zero and matched nodes toward one with the narrower goal of increasing biases for matched nodes. The result interpretations and limitations concerning noisy inputs and ambiguous annotations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation, optimizer, hyperparameter ranges, hardware, solver descriptions, and the ThinkMatch access link are retained. The PPI architecture/settings paragraph moves from page 9 to page 8 without adding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to earlier graph-matching and optimal-transport methods remain unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: The bias-loss explanation is shortened and rewritten, and a funding acknowledgement is added after Section 9. The broader narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with revised curves and fewer sweep points, table ranking highlights are adjusted, and pages 7–10 reflow. Figure 2 moves upward as the PPI settings paragraph shifts to page 8. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The revised loss accompanies small, mixed performance changes, leaving its overall benefit uncertain. Reporting consistency also weakens: Appendix B still says OPGM beats OPGM-rs on Pascal VOC, although Table 3 now reports 60.8 versus 60.9. Figure 2 shows stronger low-lambda sensitivity while the discussion still calls the effect insignificant. These possible empirical benefits and interpretation problems do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
